items.a: React (React.js) is a JavaScript library, made by Meta (Facebook), for building user interfaces of websites and web apps. You build the UI from reusable pieces called components, and React updates the page efficiently when data changes. It is the most popular frontend technology. React developers usually also know JavaScript / TypeScript, HTML, CSS, hooks, Redux and Next.js.

React Native is a framework, made by Meta, for building mobile apps for both Android and iOS from one JavaScript / TypeScript codebase, using React concepts. It is different from React (which is for websites). React Native developers know React, JavaScript / TypeScript, Redux and mobile app publishing.

Flutter is Google's framework for building mobile apps (Android and iOS), plus web and desktop apps, from one codebase. It uses the Dart programming language. Flutter developers know Dart, widgets, state management (Provider, Bloc, Riverpod) and Firebase.

Angular is a frontend framework by Google for building web applications, written in TypeScript. It is a complete framework (routing, forms, HTTP built in), popular in large enterprise projects. Note: AngularJS (version 1.x) is the old version and very different from modern Angular (2+).
Vue.js is a JavaScript framework for building web user interfaces, known for being simple to learn. It is an alternative to React and Angular. Nuxt.js is the Vue equivalent of Next.js.
Next.js is a framework built on top of React for building fast websites and web apps, with server-side rendering, routing and backend API routes built in. It is very common in modern React jobs.

JavaScript is the programming language of the web: it makes web pages interactive and runs in every browser. With Node.js it also runs on servers. React, Angular, Vue and Node.js are all based on JavaScript. Note: JavaScript is completely different from Java.

TypeScript is JavaScript with types, made by Microsoft. It catches mistakes before the code runs and is preferred in large projects. Angular uses it by default and most modern React and Node.js projects use it too.

Node.js lets JavaScript run on the server (backend), not just in the browser. It is used to build APIs and backend services, usually with Express.js or NestJS, and is the "N" in the MERN and MEAN stacks.

Java is a popular, general-purpose programming language used mostly for backend / enterprise systems (banking, e-commerce, large companies), Android apps and big data tools. Java backend developers usually work with Spring Boot, Hibernate and microservices. Java is also the most common language for Selenium test automation.

Spring Boot is the most popular Java framework for building backend applications and REST APIs quickly. It is part of the Spring ecosystem (Spring MVC, Spring Data, Spring Security). Almost every Java backend JD asks for it.

Python is an easy-to-read programming language used for backend web development (Django, FastAPI, Flask), data analysis, machine learning / AI, automation scripts and testing. It is one of the most in-demand languages.

Django is a full-featured Python web framework (admin panel, ORM, authentication built in). FastAPI is a modern, fast Python framework for building APIs. Flask is a small, lightweight Python framework. All three are used to build backends in Python.

.NET is Microsoft's platform for building web, desktop, cloud and backend applications, mostly with the C# language. ASP.NET Core is used for web apps and APIs. Modern .NET (Core, 6+) runs on Windows, Linux and Mac; the older .NET Framework runs only on Windows.
PHP is a server-side language widely used for websites. WordPress is built with PHP, and Laravel is the most popular PHP framework for building web applications.
Kotlin is the main modern language for Android apps (it replaced Java as Google's preferred choice). Swift is Apple's language for iPhone / iOS apps. Native mobile developers use one of these.

Selenium is the most widely used tool for automating web browser testing. Testers write scripts (mostly in Java, also Python, C# or JavaScript) that open a browser, click, type and check results automatically. Selenium WebDriver is the main part; it is usually combined with TestNG / JUnit and Cucumber.

Cypress and Playwright are modern web test automation tools, alternatives to Selenium, mostly written in JavaScript / TypeScript. They are faster to set up and more reliable for modern web apps. Playwright (by Microsoft) supports several browsers and languages.
Appium is an open-source tool to automate testing of mobile apps on Android and iOS, using the same style as Selenium.
Apache JMeter is a free tool for performance and load testing: it simulates many users hitting an application or API at once to measure speed and find limits.
Postman is a tool to send requests to APIs and check their responses. Developers use it to test their APIs and QA engineers use it for API testing; collections can be automated with Newman.

JIRA (by Atlassian) is a tool to track work in software teams: user stories, tasks, bugs and sprints. Almost all Agile teams, developers and testers use it, often together with Confluence for documentation.

AWS (Amazon Web Services) is the biggest cloud platform: companies rent servers (EC2), storage (S3), databases (RDS), serverless functions (Lambda) and more instead of buying hardware. Microsoft Azure and Google Cloud (GCP) are the main alternatives.
Microsoft Azure is Microsoft's cloud platform, the second biggest after AWS, popular with companies using Microsoft products (.NET, Office 365, Active Directory).
Jenkins is a popular open-source tool for CI/CD: it automatically builds, tests and deploys code whenever developers push changes.
Terraform (by HashiCorp) is an Infrastructure as Code tool: engineers write code to create and manage cloud servers, networks and databases on AWS, Azure or GCP, instead of clicking in a console.
Apache Kafka is a system for sending large streams of messages / events between applications in real time. It is common in microservices, banking and data engineering roles.
MongoDB is a popular NoSQL database that stores data as flexible JSON-like documents instead of tables. It is the "M" in the MERN / MEAN stacks.

SQL (Structured Query Language) is the language used to store, read and change data in relational databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle and SQL Server. Developers, testers and data analysts all use it.
Redis is a very fast in-memory data store, mostly used as a cache to speed up applications, and for sessions and queues.
Power BI is Microsoft's tool for building business dashboards and reports from data. Tableau is a similar tool. Data analysts and BI developers use them, with DAX formulas in Power BI.
Linux is a free operating system that runs most servers and cloud machines. DevOps, cloud, backend and system admin roles need Linux command-line skills.
GraphQL is a way of building APIs where the client asks for exactly the data it needs in one request. It is an alternative to REST APIs, created by Meta.

items.q: What is Generative AI and LLM?
items.a: Generative AI creates new content (text, images, code). An LLM (Large Language Model) such as GPT, Claude, Gemini or Llama is the AI model behind chat assistants. RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) means the AI first searches your own documents and then answers from them, like this assistant. GenAI developer roles need Python, LLM APIs, prompt engineering, vector databases and LangChain / LlamaIndex.
